Tiers, drops, Uniques, checks

How tier, level and ascension show on a model without a new mesh, how a drive lies on the floor, the sixteen Uniques, the keystone and active marks, and the legibility tests at real size.

Tier, level and ascension on the model

Three things, three different places: tier is a ring under the form, level is size and glow, ascension is a gold star in a ring over it. The family outline between them is never covered. Yellow tags mark what would be better done in a shader; each has a geometry-only version, which is what is drawn.

Tier: a ring is added under the form, the body never changes

Commonplain body
Rarea white ring
Epica foil ring, a spark
QuicksilverEpic
Better as a shader
The Epic foil. A view-angle rainbow on the ring that moves as the drive rocks. Without shaders: the ring's 14 segments take the six foil rows in turn and the ring spins, so the colours travel.

Level 1 to 3: size and glow, one step each

Level 1size x1.0
Level 2x1.15, seams lit
Level 3x1.3, core pulses
Better as a shader
The glow steps. A rim light whose strength is the level, pulsing at 3. Without shaders: size alone carries it (x1.0, x1.15, x1.3) and the hot row is baked one step brighter per level. Levels 4 to 9 keep the level 3 size.

Level 5, ascended: one rule for every drive. Gold seams, and a gold star in a ring over its head

Better as a shader
The halo. A soft additive glow round the star with slow turning rays, the star as a sprite. Without shaders: a 12-segment gold ring and a twenty-triangle star 0.4 over the form, as drawn. The hot row swaps to the gold row either way. Tier sits under the form and ascension over it, so an ascended Epic (Steam, last) shows both and the family outline stays clear between them.

The floor drop and the fly-in

Step 7's drop, with the model in the badge's place: the white disc stays behind it so it reads on any stage, the sunny rings stay on the floor, the name tag stays above. The model bobs 2 px and rocks; it does not spin edge-on. Taken, the disc pops away in 6 frames, the model arcs to its orbit slot in 30, and the chip it lands on gets the sunny ring.
On the floor. White disc r 15 behind the model, centre 27 px over the floor. Model 22 px. Sunny rings 21 x 6.5 and 33 x 10. Name tag 20 px above. The tier ring shows under the form.

Fly-in. Frames 0 to 6 the disc shrinks away. Frames 0 to 30 the model arcs to its slot, 62 px high at the middle, with a dotted sunny trail. Frame 30: the sunny ring on its HUD chip, 90 frames.

The glass shell of the built pickups is dropped: the disc does its job and does not hide the shape.

Uniques: the seventh treatment, for no family

A Unique is dark where every family drive is bright. Body: near black with one metal or earth colour of its own (none of the six family colours, nor coral, lagoon or sunny). Edge: ink and then white, where a family drive has ink only. Badge: cut as a diamond, black face, rim in its own colour, one diamond pip in place of three level pips. Each has one living material, drawn here as a still; all sixteen need the custom shader, and without it they fall back to the dark body, the double edge and a slow sheen baked into the atlas.
Puppeteer
Every 25% dealt: fires the drive to its left.
Material: Threads that glow in a pulse travelling to the left. It says: I pull that one.
Ashbank
Heat lost to hits: banked, and returned on your next KO.
Material: An inner glow that rises with the banked Heat; ash drifts in. It says: How much is saved.
Changing of the Guard
Tag in: the new fighter lands as a blast, 10%.
Material: A brass sheen that flashes edge to edge when the tag is ready. It says: Tag now.
Turnabout
A cash-out: your row reverses. The new first drive fills.
Material: Sand that flows upward after each flip. It says: Which way the row reads.
Mockingbird
Always: becomes the last drive a foe fired at you.
Material: A dissolve edge that eats the grey and shows the copied form. It says: Empty or loaded, and with what.
Hundred-Year Seed
From loop 3: fires +10%, doubling every loop.
Material: Growth rings lit from inside, one more band each loop. It says: How many loops it has grown.
Lifeline Coin
Your last stock lost: pay 150 coins and keep it.
Material: Iridescent foil that goes dull when the purse is under the price. It says: You can afford one.
Kiln
A KO: keeps all your Heat. Heat drains 3 a second.
Material: A heat-haze halo that bends the air around it, always sinking. It says: Heat is draining.
Absolution
Always: your first keystone has no price.
Material: A slow pearl sweep across the break while the price is off. It says: The price is lifted now.
Clockwork Heel
An L-cancel: fills the drive to its right.
Material: An animated gear pattern that ticks, and stops during the 3-second gate. It says: Ready or winding.
Hair Trigger
Your active: costs 40 Heat, not pips.
Material: Sparks along the edge, denser when Heat can pay for more uses. It says: Uses in hand.
Shared Flame
With a partner: one Heat meter, filled by both.
Material: A liquid-metal flow from one ring to the other, toward whoever gained last. It says: Who is feeding the meter.
Pied Piper
A popped enemy: fights for you for 10 seconds.
Material: A soft note-shaped trail behind each ally. It says: Which enemies are yours.
Fool's Gold
Every 10 coins held: your fires deal 1% more.
Material: A glitter that scales with the purse and goes flat after a shop. It says: How rich, so how strong.
Albatross
Offstage: damage refills your jumps. No Heat is lost.
Material: A wind-streak trail that appears only offstage. It says: You are in its element.
Ouroboros
A chain's last link: also charges your first drive.
Material: A scale pattern that runs once round the ring for each returned charge. It says: The loop closed.
BoltEvery 30% dealt: lightning strikes the
HexEvery 50% dealt: 3% and the foe is Mar
RushEvery 40% dealt: Haste for 5 seconds.
PuppeteerEvery 25% dealt: fires the drive to its left. One of a kind. It has no family and no levels.
A Take (replaces your Unique) B Leave it
In orbit. It does not ride the row's ring. It takes its own path tilted 35 degrees, turning the other way, a fifth larger, leaving a short light trail, so one glance finds it. Its slot in the HUD row is still its place in the chain.
On the floor. A black diamond plate where a drive has a white disc, white rings where a drive has sunny ones, and a thin column of light 150 px tall so it can be found from across the stage.
In the pick list. Its own beat: the three ordinary tags clear, one dark tag slides in larger with its material running and the burst "A Unique", and input is held half a second.

Keystones and actives

Keystones stay grape-ink wedges; each of the eight has its own emblem on a white disc (five were drawn in earlier steps, Overclock, Twin Soul and All In are new). Awakened: the wedge turns sunny, as "Set!" does, and the emblem disc gains a sunny second ring and a white spark, so it still reads on the 32 px HUD wedge. Actives are the drive badge cut square in cobalt, a colour no family uses, each with its own glyph.

Drives charge twice as fast.

Drives charge x3.

The five actives: the badge at 46 px and the 22 px HUD chip
Volley3 pips. Three darts in a line: the whole row, one after another.
Overdrive3 pips. A gauge with its needle past the top.
Detonate2 pips. A burst with a core: the words go off.
Recall2 pips. An arrow that turns back.
Double Down4 pips. Two chevrons down: the stake, doubled.

What to decide

1. The six languagesTall and pointed, six-sided, wide and open, ringed, flat-topped and heavy, counted pieces. If one of these is wrong the drives under it change, so this comes first.
2. The ink edge on modelsEvery model on these sheets has an ink outline, which is what makes a 24 px drive read on any stage. It costs a second copy of each mesh (or one outline shader). Without it the bright stages lose the pale families.
3. Facing the cameraThe models are flat reliefs, as the six built ones are. They rock 12 degrees and never spin edge-on. A full spin would hide the shape half the time.
4. The weakest shapesJet Trail, Nova, Slick, Static, Contagion and Clockwork Heel are the ones least sure to read at 22 px. Look at those chips first in the rows above.
5. UniquesThe diamond badge and the dark body are the class. Shared Flame was briefed as two linked rings, which is Utility's own mark, so it is drawn as a figure of eight. Albatross and Ouroboros lean on Sky and Tempo shapes and rely on the dark body to stand apart.
6. ShadersThree ordinary treatments are tagged as better in a shader, each with a version that needs none. The sixteen Unique materials have no good geometry-only version: they wait on the shader study.
